lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Sort into headings Sun / Safety: angle low; wear a hat; measure stick; never stare at sun.

FEEDBACK

CHECK
Pasting full sentences from a site into notes risks plagiarism later.
lesson.independent_task:

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Make eight own-word notes from at least two sources under your headings. Tag sources and cut duplicates. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: original example using notes on new material; names a specific word, source or choice and explains its effect.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample error: Pasting full sentences from a site into notes risks plagiarism later.. Correction: Sun: angle low; measure stick.. Why it helps the audience is stated.

Parent: Likely misconception: Pasting full sentences from a site into notes risks plagiarism later. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating notes on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with notes, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept original work about notes with a specific supporting detail. Reject copied model wording with no new material. / Accept a misconception, a correction, and a purpose-linked reason for notes. Reject corrections that do not change the inaccurate idea..

teach_steps.explain:
Making notes means short own-word cues under headings, with source tags, then organising so drafting is not copy-paste.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
